recommendations: Test the challenger cutoff. Send 10% of applications to the challenger at the champion bad rate (Step 7). Add a small random test below the cutoff to measure the applicants that the data does not contain (Step 7).
Test a higher price for the grades with a negative NPV. The 2015 prices did not pay for the risk: 32 of 35 sub-grades lost money (Part 2: Pricing).
Plan the losses with the lifetime default rate, not the current rate. The 2018 vintage shows 2.7% to date, but its forecast is 12.8% (Part 2: Loss forecast).
Do not build a recovery model. A rank by balance gives the same dollars. Test a sale of the debt against in-house collection (Part 2: Recoveries).
answer: Yes. At the champion bad rate of 12.5%, the challenger approves 85.7% of the 2015 applicants against 84.5% for the champion. On the 2015 loans, it adds $7.1M of realized NPV, and at least $5.1M for each cost assumption that we tested. But the 2015 book lost money at its prices, so the cutoff must go together with a pricing test.
